resources.string: Listening — devices nearby running this module will appear here within the 8-second window
Mesh not running — nodes heard in the last 8 seconds will show here after start
Waiting for messages — nearby devices running this module relay each other\'s broadcasts; messages you send also appear here
Not running — received messages will appear here in reverse chronological order after start
Up to 18 chars · plaintext broadcast · no receipt
[!] Beyond the %1$d-char limit; the message will be truncated on send

Each broadcast packet is 31B: the MESH|ID|seq|ttl| header takes 16-19B, leaving about 5-8B for text (about 5-8 ASCII chars, 1-3 Chinese chars). The input limit is 18 chars; sends are truncated by bytes.
Typical range 10-50m (open ground, no obstruction); initial TTL is 2, so a message travels at most 2 more hops, and each device relays a given message only once.
Broadcast in plaintext throughout — no encryption, no authentication, no delivery receipt: any BLE scanner in range can read the content.
Sending uses 3 rounds × 1-second broadcast windows at about 3 seconds per message; a relayed message\'s RSSI is the forwarding node\'s signal to this device, not the original sender\'s distance.
A node is considered offline after 8 seconds without broadcasts; the local ID is randomly generated alphanumeric and persisted, not derived from hardware identifiers.
